title: Kernels and cokernels of modules on a flat algebraic-space groupoid
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]: its test-scheme points form groupoids, naturally in the test scheme, with source $s$, target $t$, identity $e$, inverse $i$, and composition $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$, first the second arrow and then the first. Suppose $s,t$ are flat, meaning flat on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Modules on an algebraic space are on its small etale ringed site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with quasi-coherence as in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and tensor pullback along maps of algebraic spaces as in [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], [def-pc-module-pullback]. Define $\mathcal C$ to have objects $(M,\alpha)$ with $M$ a quasi-coherent module on $U$ and $\alpha:t^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}s^*M$, satisfying $e^*\alpha=1$ and $c^*\alpha=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\alpha\circ\operatorname{pr}_0^*\alpha$ under the canonical pullback identifications. A morphism $v:(M,\alpha)\to(N,\beta)$ is a module map with $s^*v\circ\alpha=\beta\circ t^*v$. Then $\mathcal C$ is abelian [def-sp-abelian]. Its forgetful functor to quasi-coherent modules on $U$ is additive and faithful, reflects isomorphisms, and computes kernels and cokernels as the ordinary small-etale module-sheaf kernels and cokernels on $U$, endowed with their induced groupoid isomorphisms. In particular these underlying kernels and cokernels are quasi-coherent. No quasi-compactness, finite-presentation, separation or Noetherian hypothesis on the spaces or their maps is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06VZ (lemma-abelian), statement and proof: the induced kernel and cokernel isomorphisms; additivity, faithfulness and reflection of isomorphisms from the displayed definition of morphisms.

proof.text: The ambient category of module sheaves on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ is abelian by [lem-pur-ringed-site-module-category-abelian]. Sums and negatives of equivariant maps remain equivariant, by linearity of tensor pullback. The zero module with its unique descent is a zero object. The module $M\oplus N$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]; its descent is $\alpha\oplus\beta$, with the pullback identifications obtained from $b\otimes(m,n)\mapsto(b\otimes m,b\otimes n)$. Its inclusions and projections are equivariant and satisfy the biproduct equations. Thus $\mathcal C$ is additive. The forgetful functor is additive and faithful by its definition on morphisms. If $v$ is an underlying isomorphism, multiply $s^*v\,\alpha=\beta\,t^*v$ by its inverses to obtain $s^*(v^{-1})\,\beta=\alpha\,t^*(v^{-1})$. It therefore reflects isomorphisms.

For an equivariant $v:(M,\alpha)\to(N,\beta)$ put $j:K=\ker v\to M$ and $q:N\to Q=\operatorname{coker}v$ in all module sheaves. Both $K,Q$ are quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]. For each flat algebraic-space map $h$, [lem-sfb-space-flat-etale-ringed-comparison] says that its structural ring sheaf is flat over the inverse-image ring; [lem-sfb-flat-ringed-topos-pullback-exact] then makes the ringed tensor pullback $L_h=\mathcal O\otimes_{h^{-1}\mathcal O}h^{-1}(-)$ exact, and the natural isomorphism $\tau_h:h^*\simeq L_h$ of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization] transfers exactness to the chart tensor pullback $h^*$. In particular $s^*j,t^*j$ are kernels of $s^*v,t^*v$, while $s^*q,t^*q$ are their cokernels. The isomorphisms $\alpha,\beta$ identify these two arrow diagrams. Kernel and cokernel universal properties give unique maps $\kappa:t^*K\to s^*K$ and $\lambda:t^*Q\to s^*Q$ with $s^*j\,\kappa=\alpha\,t^*j$ and $\lambda\,t^*q=s^*q\,\beta$. Applying the same construction to $\alpha^{-1},\beta^{-1}$ gives inverses: the composites are identities by uniqueness in those universal properties.

Use the canonical composition comparisons of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization]. Their coherence follows on local iterated tensors: both reassociations send $a\otimes(b\otimes(c\otimes m))$ to $a\,h^\sharp(b)\,(kh)^\sharp(c)\otimes m$; the identity comparison sends $a\otimes m$ to $am$. These local formulas determine the sheaf maps. Pull back $s^*j\,\kappa=\alpha\,t^*j$ by $e$. Since $se=te=1_U$ and $e^*\alpha=1$, this gives $j\,e^*\kappa=j$; cancel the monomorphism $j$. Pulling back $\lambda\,t^*q=s^*q\,\beta$ gives $e^*\lambda\,q=q$; cancel the epimorphism $q$. Thus the identity laws hold without requiring $e$ to be flat.

Put $P=R\times_{s,U,t}R$, with projections $p_0,p_1$. They are base changes of $t,s$, respectively. Flatness is stable under base change and composition by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], applied to algebraic spaces. Thus $sc=sp_1$ and $tc=tp_0$ are flat. By the flat-pullback conclusion of step 2, $(sc)^*j$ is monic and $(tc)^*q$ is epic. Under the coherent identifications of step 3 the defining equations of $\kappa$ give
$$(sc)^*j\,c^*\kappa=c^*\alpha\,(tc)^*j,$$
$$ (sc)^*j\,(p_1^*\kappa\circ p_0^*\kappa)=(p_1^*\alpha\circ p_0^*\alpha)\,(tc)^*j.$$
The right sides agree by the cocycle law for $\alpha$, so cancellation proves the law for $\kappa$. For $\lambda$ its defining equation gives
$$c^*\lambda\,(tc)^*q=(sc)^*q\,c^*\beta,$$
$$ (p_1^*\lambda\circ p_0^*\lambda)\,(tc)^*q=(sc)^*q\,(p_1^*\beta\circ p_0^*\beta).$$
Cancel $(tc)^*q$ and use the law for $\beta$. Consequently $(K,\kappa)$ and $(Q,\lambda)$ are objects of $\mathcal C$, and $j,q$ are equivariant.

Let $(L,\delta)$ be any object and $a:L\to M$ equivariant with $va=0$. There is a unique underlying $b:L\to K$ with $jb=a$. To check equivariance compare $s^*b\,\delta$ and $\kappa\,t^*b$ after the monomorphism $s^*j$: both composites equal $\alpha\,t^*a$ by the equations for $a,j$. Hence $b$ is equivariant, and uniqueness is inherited from module sheaves. This proves the kernel universal property in $\mathcal C$. Dually, for an equivariant $a:N\to L$ with $av=0$, let $b:Q\to L$ satisfy $bq=a$. Compare $s^*b\,\lambda$ and $\delta\,t^*b$ after precomposition with the epimorphism $t^*q$: both are $\delta\,t^*a$. This proves equivariance and the cokernel universal property. Thus the forgetful functor computes both constructions as claimed.

For any $v$, form $\operatorname{Coim}v=\operatorname{coker}(\ker v\to M)$ and $\operatorname{Im}v=\ker(N\to\operatorname{coker}v)$ inside $\mathcal C$. Their canonical comparison is equivariant by the kernel and cokernel factorizations of step 5. Under forgetting it is the usual coimage-to-image isomorphism in the ambient abelian module category, hence is an isomorphism by step 1. If $v$ is monic in $\mathcal C$, its kernel inclusion is zero (cancel $v$), hence its kernel object is zero; its coimage is $M$. The comparison consequently identifies $v$ with the kernel of its cokernel. Dually every epic $v$ is the cokernel of its kernel. Together with additivity and the kernels and cokernels already constructed this is precisely [def-sp-abelian]. No finiteness or separation hypothesis entered any step.
